ai.literal: By action feeling ashamed is shame indeed; beautiful forehead good women's modesty is other.
ai.translation: True shame is shrinking away from wrongful deeds. The natural modesty of beautiful women is something else entirely.
ai.modern: தகாத செயல்களைச் செய்ய வெட்கப்படுவதே உண்மையான நாணம் ஆகும். அழகிய நெற்றியை உடைய பெண்களின் இயல்பான நாணம் என்பது அதிலிருந்து வேறுபட்டதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet distinguishes true moral shame from natural feminine modesty. The word 'கருமத்தால்' (by action) emphasizes that genuine shame is the internal shrinking away from committing dishonorable or wrong deeds. In contrast, the natural shyness seen in beautiful women is merely a physical or social trait, which is entirely different from this noble virtue.

ai.literal: Food, clothing, other things, to living beings all, different are not; modesty possession human beings' distinction.
ai.translation: Food, clothing, and other such things are not different for all living beings. The possession of modesty is the special distinction of human beings.
ai.modern: உணவு, உடை மற்றும் பிற தேவைகள் எல்லா உயிர்களுக்கும் பொதுவானவை. ஆனால் நாணம் என்னும் பண்பைக் கொண்டிருப்பதே மனிதர்களுக்கு உரிய சிறப்பம்சமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the basic physical needs of life with the moral quality of modesty. The words 'ஊண்' (food), 'உடை' (clothing), and 'எச்சம்' (the rest) represent necessities that all living beings share, making them common to all. The true distinction ('சிறப்பு') of human beings ('மாந்தர்') lies in 'நாணுடைமை', the possession of a sense of shame or moral modesty. It is this inner quality that elevates humans above other creatures.

ai.literal: Flesh depending-on life all; modesty called goodness it-depends-on perfection.
ai.translation: All life depends on the physical body; true perfection depends on the goodness called modesty.
ai.modern: எல்லா உயிர்களும் உடம்பை அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்டு வாழ்கின்றன; அதுபோல சான்றாண்மை என்பது நாணம் என்னும் நற்பண்பை அடிப்படையாகக் கொண்டு வாழ்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The couplet draws a direct parallel between physical existence and moral excellence. Just as all living beings rely on their physical flesh to exist in this world, true perfection relies entirely on the virtue of modesty. The word 'குறித்த' means to be stationed in or to depend upon, showing the foundational nature of these elements. Without the body, life cannot manifest, and without a sense of shame for wrongdoings, noble excellence cannot survive.

ai.literal: Ornament - is it not - modesty - possessing - to the noble ones - that - if without - disease - is it not - proud - walk.
ai.translation: Is not modesty the true ornament of the noble? Without it, is not a proud bearing merely a disease?
ai.modern: நாணத்தை உடையவராக இருப்பதே சான்றோர்களுக்கு உண்மையான அழகாகும். அந்த நாணம் இல்லாவிட்டால், அவர்கள் பெருமிதத்துடன் நடக்கும் நடை ஒரு நோயே அல்லவா?
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the true beauty of noble people with a false sense of greatness. The word 'நாண்' (modesty or a shrinking from wrongdoing) is described as the defining 'அணி' (ornament) for the noble ('சான்றோர்'). If they lack this quality ('அஃது இன்றேல்'), their 'பீடு நடை' (proud or stately bearing) is no longer a mark of greatness. Instead, it becomes a 'பிணி' (disease or affliction), something unnatural and harmful. The rhetorical questions ('அன்றோ') emphasize that true dignity comes from inner modesty, not outward arrogance.

ai.literal: Others' disgrace and their own disgrace, those who feel ashamed of - to modesty, dwelling place, will say the world.
ai.translation: The world will call those who shrink from the disgrace of others as much as their own, the very abode of modesty.
ai.modern: பிறருக்கு வரும் பழியையும் தமக்கு வரும் பழியையும் கண்டு வெட்கப்படுகின்றவர்களை, நாணம் தங்கியிருக்கும் உறைவிடம் என்று உலகம் சொல்லும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the highest standard of modesty or a sense of shame. It states that true modesty is not just avoiding one's own disgrace, but also feeling ashamed when others face disgrace. The word 'நாணுவார்' refers to those who instinctively shrink from any shameful act, regardless of who commits it. The world considers such empathetic and principled people to be the very dwelling place ('உறைபதி') of modesty itself.

ai.literal: Modesty fence without-having indeed vast world they-will-not-cherish high-ones.
ai.translation: The noble ones will not desire even the vast world if it means living without the fence of modesty.
ai.modern: மேன்மையானவர்கள் நாணம் என்னும் வேலியை விட்டுவிட்டு, இந்தப் பரந்த உலகத்தை ஆள்வதையும் விரும்ப மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that noble people value modesty above all worldly possessions. The word 'நாண்' (modesty or a sense of shame against doing wrong) is compared to a protective 'வேலி' (fence) that guards their character. The phrase 'கொள்ளாது... பேணலர்' indicates that without maintaining this fence, they would not cherish even the vast world ('வியன் ஞாலம்'). Thus, true greatness lies in preserving one's moral boundaries rather than acquiring limitless power or wealth.

ai.translation: Those who truly possess modesty will give up their lives for its sake, but they will never give up their modesty for the sake of their lives.

ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of modesty or moral dignity. The phrase 'நாண் ஆள்பவர்' refers to those who have mastered and truly possess this virtue. For them, modesty is far more precious than life itself. Consequently, they would willingly sacrifice their lives to preserve their sense of shame, but they would never abandon their modesty merely to survive.

ai.translation: If a person is not ashamed of what makes others ashamed, virtue itself will find fit cause to be ashamed of him.
ai.modern: பிறர் வெட்கப்பட வேண்டிய பழிச்செயலுக்கு ஒருவன் தான் வெட்கப்படாமல் இருப்பானானால், அறமே அவனைக் கண்டு வெட்கப்பட்டு விலகும் தன்மையை அது பெறும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines true modesty as aligning one's moral compass with the conscience of the wider community. It warns that a person must feel ashamed of actions that others rightfully consider shameful. If someone brazenly commits such acts without personal shame ('தான் நாணான் ஆயின்'), they completely detach themselves from moral goodness. As a result, virtue ('அறம்') itself will feel ashamed to be associated with them and will abandon them.

ai.literal: Lineage it will burn, principle if failed; goodness it will burn, shamelessness stood state.
ai.translation: Failing in one's principles will destroy one's lineage. But shamelessness, if it takes root, will destroy every goodness one possesses.
ai.modern: ஒருவன் தன் கொள்கையிலிருந்து தவறினால் அது அவனது குலத்தின் பெருமையை அழிக்கும். ஆனால் அவனிடம் நாணமற்ற தன்மை நிலைத்து நின்றால், அது அவனது நற்பண்புகள் அனைத்தையும் அழித்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the damage caused by a lapse in principles with the devastation caused by a lack of modesty. If a person fails to uphold their ideals, it brings ruin to their family's reputation. However, if shamelessness takes permanent hold of a person, it burns away every other virtue and goodness they might have. The word 'nāṇ' here specifically means a noble sense of shame or modesty, fitting the chapter's theme. The repetition of the word 'cuṭum' (will burn) emphasizes the destructive power of both flaws, showing that shamelessness is the ultimate destroyer of personal character.

ai.literal: Modesty inside those who have not, movement, wooden puppet by string life having deceived like that.
ai.translation: The actions of those who have no modesty in their hearts are like a wooden puppet creating the illusion of life by means of a string.
ai.modern: மனதில் நாணம் இல்லாதவர்களின் செயல்பாடுகள், கயிற்றினால் இயக்கப்படும் மரப்பாவை உயிருள்ளது போல மயக்கத்தை ஏற்படுத்துவதைப் போன்றது.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a brilliant pun on the word 'நாண்', which means both 'modesty' and 'string'. It compares people who lack inner modesty to wooden puppets. Just as a puppet seems alive only because it is pulled by a string, shameless people merely go through the motions of life without true human dignity. Their outward actions are just an illusion of living.
